messages:
Ava Morgan: Heads-up team 0min sync: need three battlecard soundbites for webinar follow-up + inbound routing rules. Keep each line <20 words.

Samir Desai: Draft soundbites: 
1) Cloud AI platforms: 'Hosted ease, but opaque unit economics. We give you predictable cost + multi-environment portability.'
2) LLM APIs: 'Access models without building serving infra; runtime optimizations cut token cost and tail latency.'
3) Infra vendors: 'Integrated serving runtime + orchestration 0x less ops glue for SLOs.'

Claire O'Neil: Good. Add micro-proof hooks: 'see p99 numbers' and 'dedicated pool case study' placeholders so sales can cite evidence.

Ava Morgan: Routing rules quick: keywords->route mapping. If 'on-prem' or 'vpc' -> enterprise@redwood.com; if 'latency' or 'p99' -> infra-sales@redwood.com; if 'cost' or 'billing' -> pricing@redwood.com; else growth@redwood.com. Include fallback cadence in playbook.

Samir Desai: Two A/B email subjects for follow-up: A) 'How much could runtime batching save you?' B) 'Can your provider hold 99th-pctl latency during bursts?' We'll run 2-week conversion test.

OpsRouterBot: New lead routed -> route: infra-sales@redwood.com, score: 69, matched: ['p99','latency']

Claire O'Neil: Objection scripts (one-liners for SDR paste): 
- 'Managed is simpler' -> 'We match manageability AND offer an exit path to private/dedicated without a rewrite.'
- 'Self-hosted is cheaper' -> 'Often hides ops risk; our Dedicated gives price predictability with SLA-backed capacity.'

Ava Morgan: Perfect. Action items: Samir add exact benchmark numbers and cite the case study link; Claire draft 3 rebuttal bullets per competitor; I'll assemble final one-pager and drop in the playbook for sign-off by EOD.
